messages:

Subject: Hosting territory confirmation + VPC details request

Hi Tessa,

Thanks for taking this. We're working through the SIG/CAIQ collection for our internal security review and need explicit confirmation on a few items before we can clear Redwood for production on Zephyr Health workloads. Our primary concerns:

- Can you confirm which AWS regions Redwood will host our production model inference when we select EU-only hosting (we need the canonical region names, e.g., eu-west-1)?
- For Private deployment / Private Connect: do you support VPC peering or AWS PrivateLink into a customer VPC? Any constraints on partner-managed endpoints?
- KMS: can keys be customer-managed (BYOK) and reside in our account/HSM?
- Data egress: an explicit statement that production inference logs/outputs will not be transferred outside the selected region (EU).

We also need a simple network diagram and a short implementation note for our procurement and security teams. Our timeline: final attestation by 2026-11-18.

Appreciate a short written confirmation and any attachments you can share.

Best,
Gina
Gina Lopez
Security Program Manager
Zephyr Health

[Attachment: SIG-questionnaire-refs.xlsx (spreadsheet, 120KB)]

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.example.com>

Subject: Re: Hosting territory confirmation + VPC details request

Hi Gina — thanks for the clear ask. Quick answers below and I attached an initial implementation note + diagram.

Summary answers (short):
- Region: For EU-only hosting we pin production inference to eu-west-1 (Ireland). We support locking model-serving to a single region per workload.
- Private connectivity: Redwood supports AWS PrivateLink (recommended) and VPC peering in select configurations. PrivateLink is our preferred pattern for customer VPCs as it eliminates route table changes on the customer side.
- KMS/BYOK: We support BYOK where the customer provisions a KMS key in their account and grants Redwood a restricted IAM principal for encryption operations. If you require HSM-backed keys, we can work with AWS CloudHSM or external HSM providers — we typically validate via a short onboarding checklist.
- Data egress: When a workload is pinned to EU-only hosting and uses Private Connect, production inference traffic and model KV caches remain in eu-west-1. Diagnostic logs can be forwarded to a customer bucket in the same region; we do not replicate data outside the region unless explicitly requested.

Attachments: vpc-implementation-notes-20261110.pdf (short runbook + diagram), kms-byok-diagram.png

Next steps I propose:
1) I'll send a formal region-assurance statement that you can share with procurement (by 2026-11-12).
2) If you'd like, we can schedule a 30-minute tech sync early next week to walk the network diagram and onboarding steps.

Cheers,
Tessa Morgan
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Thanks, Tessa — that helps. A couple of clarifying items from security/procurement:

> - Region: For EU-only hosting we pin production inference to eu-west-1 (Ireland).

Can you provide the exact AZs or confirm whether multi-AZ redundancy will ever cause temporary cross-region traffic? We need to be confident there is zero cross-region egress for EU-pinned workloads.

> - KMS/BYOK: We support BYOK where the customer provisions a KMS key in their account and grants Redwood a restricted IAM principal for encryption operations.

Is the cryptographic operation performed in our account (i.e., Redwood calls kms:Encrypt/Decrypt in our account) or is the key wrapped and copied into Redwood's account? We prefer KMS operations to occur in our account so keys never leave our tenancy.

> - Data egress: ... we do not replicate data outside the region unless explicitly requested.

Can you produce a short one-paragraph attestation we can include in the CAIQ/SIG answer grid and a network diagram labeled with the endpoints? Also please confirm log retention and whether you can push audit logs (S3 access logs / CloudTrail) to our S3 bucket in eu-west-1.

Thanks — procurement is waiting on the attestation and a signed statement would speed approvals.

Gina

[Quoted message above]

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.example.com>

Subject: Re: Region assurance and private connect plan for Zephyr Health

Hi Gina — attaching the formal Region Assurance Statement and a labeled diagram. Short answers here and the formal language is in the PDF attachment (region-assurance-statement-zephyr-20261112.pdf).

Key commitments (summary):
1) Region residency: Redwood confirms that Zephyr Health production inference workloads can be deployed and pinned to a single AWS region (eu-west-1). We will not move production inference traffic or persistent model-derived artifacts to another region without written authorization from Zephyr Health.

2) AZ / redundancy: Redwood uses multi-AZ deployment within the specified region for availability only. Multi-AZ operation does not cause cross-region traffic. There is no cross-region replication for EU-pinned workloads.

3) KMS / BYOK: Cryptographic operations are performed against the KMS key in the customers AWS account. Redwood issues requests that call kms:Encrypt/kms:Decrypt in the customer account — keys remain in the customer's tenancy. For HSM-backed keys, Redwood can integrate with AWS CloudHSM or customer-supplied HSM via supported AWS KMS custom key stores; this is covered in the onboarding checklist.

4) Logs and audit forwarding: We can configure CloudTrail and model audit logs to be forwarded to a customer-owned S3 bucket in the same region (eu-west-1). Log retention and lifecycle policies are under customer control. We also provide an audit log export (gzipped) on request for compliance reviews.

5) SOC 2 / CAIQ references: Redwood's SOC 2 scope covers production inference and the private connectivity options. We have filled the relevant CAIQ answers for network isolation; see attached evidence pack.

Attachments included: region-assurance-statement-zephyr-20261112.pdf (formal attestation, signed by Head of Security), kms-byok-diagram.png (labeled), vpc-implementation-notes-20261110.pdf (previous runbook)

If that aligns with your requirements I'll ask security to sign the attestation and I can provide a short insertion-ready paragraph for the CAIQ grid. Want me to draft that paragraph and the Proc/Legal-friendly line for procurement?

Best regards,

Tessa Morgan
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
